_comment: Product bugs and documentation differences found by the OUT specs (tests/e2e/specs/output). Same schema as tests/e2e/known-bugs.json; the orchestrator merges the entries. support/output/bugs.ts (outBug) reads this file until they are merged: an `open` entry makes the test named in `test` an expected failure. Entries without a marked test (severity info) document a difference between docs/testing.md and the product that the specs already assert as implemented. Evidence files are written by the specs to tests/e2e/.output/<project>/results/ (git-ignored), traces and screenshots of a failing run to .output/<project>/artifacts/ (run with E2E_BUG_REPORT=1 to get the raw failure of an open entry).

OUT-01.title: A cut to a scene whose camera is not in the program shows 1-5 frames (16-95 ms) of the empty scene ground (rgb 13,17,23) before the picture: the new <video> has no decoded frame when its layer appears
OUT-01.test: E2E-SWITCH-09 [output, cut, no dark frame] (specs/output/out-transitions.spec.ts); E2E-SWITCH-09 [output, cut, picture within N ms] guards the timing and the LOW-layer floor
OUT-01.steps: 1. Two phones K1, K2 publish a camera; scene A = K1 full canvas, scene B = K2 full canvas; start the broadcast; open /o/{slug}?k={key} (1280x720). 2. POST /api/productions/{id}/program {sceneId: B, transition: cut}, then back to A, 50 times, 800 ms apart. 3. Record every animation frame (requestAnimationFrame: layers, item state, video.readyState/videoWidth, luminance of the picture) and a CDP screencast of the page.
OUT-01.expected: E2E-SWITCH-09 / plan section 2 «Vorladen fürs Umschalten»: in every frame after a switch the item rectangle has a mean luminance >= 20; at switch time the target <video> already has readyState >= 2 and videoWidth > 0 (preloaded).
OUT-01.actual: The new SceneLayer is built with a brand-new <video> (ItemView -> MediaView -> provider.attach). Until the first frame is decoded the item is transparent over the scene ground #0d1117 (luma 16.5). 50 cuts: 47 of 50 cuts had at least one dark frame in the screencast (rgb 13,17,23 in the item rectangle), 1 animation frame without picture in the median, 4 at p95, 5 at most; the first picture appears 28 ms (p50), 67 ms (p95), 94 ms (max) after the layer; the new video has readyState 0 at insertion in most cuts. Fades are not affected (the new layer starts at opacity 0 over the old picture).
OUT-01.evidence: tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/results/out-switch-09-dark-frames.json (per cut: animation frames without picture, readyState and width at insertion; screencast frames below luma 20) and out-switch-09-cut.json (timing p50/p95/max, frames without picture)
OUT-01.fix: Keep a decoding <video> per source of the other scenes in the DOM (hidden, not display:none) and move it into the new layer like MediaPool already does for sources that two scenes share, or insert the new layer only after requestVideoFrameCallback / loadeddata of its videos (with a timeout of about 100 ms); fades can stay as they are.

OUT-02.title: Renaming a production does not change the subtitle of the standby slate (it is a copy of the name taken when the production was created)
OUT-02.steps: 1. Create a production "Webinar Q4" (standby slate subtitle = "Webinar Q4"), open the output (standby). 2. PATCH /api/productions/{id} {name: "Webinar Q4 neu"}.
OUT-02.expected: docs/testing.md E2E-OUT-11: «renamed production updates the subtitle live»; spec 4.2: standbySlate subtitle = production name.
OUT-02.actual: Production.Update(...) only copies the name; StandbySlate keeps the subtitle of the creation (Production.Create sets new SlateDto("Gleich geht's los", validName, null)). The output keeps showing the old name for ever; only an explicit PATCH of standbySlate changes it.
OUT-02.evidence: raw failure with E2E_BUG_REPORT=1: «subtitle follows the production name», received the old name after 5 s
OUT-02.fix: Either derive the default subtitle from the current name while the slate subtitle was never edited (store null/«use the name»), or update the subtitle in Production.Update when it still equals the old name.

OUT-03.title: The output preloads the sources of the preview scene at the lowest simulcast layer (320x180), not at the highest as spec 7 and E2E-SWITCH-10 require; after a cut the first picture is always 320 px wide
OUT-03.test: E2E-SWITCH-10 [output, preview at the highest layer] (specs/output/out-media.spec.ts)
OUT-03.steps: 1. K1 in scene A (program), K2 in scene B only; broadcast live, output open. 2. PUT /api/productions/{id}/preview {sceneId: B}. 3. Read the inbound-rtp frameWidth of K2 on the output's peer connection for 3 s.
OUT-03.expected: Spec 7: «preview scene items -> HIGH (preload before a take)»; E2E-SWITCH-10: that camera arrives at the highest layer (>= 1280 px) within 3 s of selecting the preview.
OUT-03.actual: ProgramView.preloadScenesFor puts the preview scene first, but SceneRenderer.preloadRequests asks for SMALL_PICTURE (320x180) for every preloaded scene, so K2 stays at 320x180. Consequence for the audience: after a take or cut the new camera is shown at 320 px (scaled up to the item) in 50 of 50 cuts and reaches 1280 px only 100-200 ms later.
OUT-03.evidence: raw failure with E2E_BUG_REPORT=1: «K2 reaches the highest layer (>= 1280 px) within 3 s of selecting the preview», received 320; tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/results/out-switch-09-cut.json (fullResolution: time to >= 1280 px after the layer appears, firstWidth 320 in all cuts)
OUT-03.fix: Pass the desired size of the item (or the highest layer) for the sources of the preview scene in the renderer's preload requests; keep LOW for the other scenes.

OUT-04.title: The output subscribes to every published track (autoSubscribe), also to sources that are in no scene
OUT-04.steps: 1. One camera in the program scene, one laptop screen S1 live but in no scene; output open. 2. Read the inbound-rtp video streams of the output page (remote SDP msid -> track SID).
OUT-04.expected: docs/testing.md GAP-26 / E2E-OUT-22: the output subscribes only to sources of scenes; no track and no bytes for S1.
OUT-04.actual: MediaSession connects with autoSubscribe: this.role !== 'sender' (true for the output), the provider sets LOW only for tracks without a desired size, it never unsubscribes. Two inbound video streams for one source in a scene; S1 delivered 148093 bytes (1280 px wide, a screen has no simulcast) in about 6 s. Because the output link is a bearer secret, anybody holding it can also receive sources that were never put on air.
OUT-04.fix: Connect the output with autoSubscribe: false and subscribe/unsubscribe the publications of the sources that appear in a scene (plus a server-side restriction of the output token if possible).

OUT-05.title: The uplink loss a sender reports (Regie «Verlust») is net of retransmissions: 0.1-0.3 % with 5 % and 20 % packet loss on the link, the plan expects 2-9 %
OUT-05.steps: netem loss 5 % on LiveKit (both directions) for 6 windows of 25 s with one camera on air; read GET /api/productions/{id}/telemetry after the windows.
OUT-05.expected: E2E-NET-04: Regie station «Verlust» (uplink, reported by the sender) between 2 and 9 %.
OUT-05.actual: slotTelemetry/summarizeSenderStats uses the cumulative packetsLost of the remote-inbound report over packetsSent; NACK retransmissions that arrive later reduce the cumulative count, so the figure stays near 0.3 % although 5 % of the packets were lost on the link (downlink inbound-rtp on the output: 3.5 % over the same window). The Regie hardly warns about a bad uplink.
OUT-05.evidence: tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/results/out-net-04-freeze-budget.json (uplinkLossPct 0-0.3 % vs. lossPct 4.7-5.1 % seen downlink in the same windows) and out-e2e-net-04.json
OUT-05.fix: Report loss per interval from the RTCP fraction lost (before retransmission), or document the metric as «Verlust nach Wiederholung» and adjust the plan.

OUT-06.title: With 20 % packet loss on the media path the output picture is frozen for 14-52 s of every minute, individual freezes last 3-9 s (plan: longest freeze <= 5 s hard, 2 s target) at 2-15 fps; at 5 % loss it freezes 0-52 s per minute (3 consecutive runs on a quiet machine: 26-52 s, plan: <= 2 s) at 5-14 fps
OUT-06.test: E2E-NET-05 [output, netem loss 20 %] (8 windows of 25 s, the longest freeze of any window counts) and E2E-NET-04 [freeze budget and sender report] (5 %, median of six windows) in specs/output/out-resilience.disruptive.spec.ts
OUT-06.steps: One camera on air, output open with ?latency=1; netem loss 20 % on the LiveKit container (ingress and egress) after a baseline window of 25 s without freezes; observe the picture of the output (luminance does not change = frozen) and inbound-rtp freezeCount / totalFreezesDuration for 8 windows of 25 s.
OUT-06.expected: E2E-NET-05 / T-FREEZE: picture continues, longest freeze <= 5 s (soft 2 s), full quality <= 10 s after clearing. E2E-NET-04: total freeze <= 2 s per minute, output fps >= 24.
OUT-06.actual: 20 % loss: longest still picture per window 3.1-4.8 s in some runs, 6.1 s, 7.7 s and 9.2 s in others; WebRTC freezes 18-64 per minute with 14-52 s of freeze time per minute; decoded fps 2-15; the picture drops to 320 px (once 640). The baseline window before the impairment has 0 freezes at 29 fps, so the freezes come from the impairment. 5 % loss: on a busy machine (other test stacks running) freeze time per minute was 0 / 2.7 / 2.8 / 4.8 / 7.9 / 8.4 s at 21-25 fps; on a quiet machine (machine CPU 6-10 %) three consecutive runs of six windows gave 26-52 s per minute at 5-14 fps (medians 37.6, 40.9 and 35.5 s per minute, longest still 3.1 s median and 6.1 s worst). The result is therefore not a matter of test machine load; it varies between runs and gets worse when the machine is quiet, a cause was not found. The page stays up, the picture never goes black, no incident, full quality is back 1-4 s after clearing. Experiment: a receiver jitterBufferTarget of 200 ms instead of the 50 ms of the output role lowers the number of freezes (5 %: 8-12 -> 2 per minute; 20 %: 50 -> 6-14 per minute) but not reliably their total duration (0.4-44 s per minute), so the long freezes come from loss recovery (retransmission / keyframes), not only from the buffer size.
OUT-06.evidence: tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/results/out-e2e-net-05.json, out-e2e-net-04.json and out-net-04-freeze-budget.json (per window: freezesPerMin, freezeSecondsPerMin, longestStillMs, fps, widths, lossPct, machineCpuBusyPct; baseline window); Playwright artifacts of the failed expected-fail runs under tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/artifacts/
OUT-06.fix: Open: tune the output role for lossy links (larger playout delay when packetsLost > 2 %, request keyframes earlier, prefer a lower simulcast layer sooner), or relax the T-FREEZE budget of the plan for 20 % loss.

OUT-11.title: Every program switch leaves the removed device <video> alive with its live MediaStream track: about 150 DOM nodes and one <video> element leak per switch (20 switches: 20 removed videos, 260 -> 3235 nodes), the page grows without bound during a show
OUT-11.test: E2E-NET-18 [output, soak] (specs/output/out-soak.soak.spec.ts, 20 minutes); E2E-NET-18 [output, soak, guard] covers the rest of T-MEM without the node and removed-video counts
OUT-11.steps: 1. Two cameras K1, K2; scene A = K1, scene B = K2; broadcast live; output open (no probe needed). 2. Switch A <-> B 20 times (cut and 300 ms fade alternating, 1.2 s apart). 3. In the output page: HeapProfiler.collectGarbage twice, Runtime.queryObjects(HTMLVideoElement.prototype), Performance.getMetrics Nodes.
OUT-11.expected: T-MEM: DOM nodes growth <= 5 % (hard), video elements constant (+- 0): the video count equals the item count of the current scene.
OUT-11.actual: After 20 switches 21 HTMLVideoElement objects are alive: 1 attached and 20 removed ones whose srcObject still holds a live MediaStreamTrack (detachedWithLiveTrack 20); Nodes 260 -> 3235 (+149 per switch), JS heap flat (4.3 -> 4.5 MB), listeners and documents flat. In the 3 minute soak (17 switches): nodes 868 -> 2665 -> 3412 (+28 % per minute). MediaView.dispose() only detaches the element from the provider and removes it from the DOM (device sources); unlike the asset branch it neither pauses it nor clears srcObject, so the media pipeline keeps the element, its sink and its detached ancestor chain (the whole old layer) alive.
OUT-11.evidence: tests/e2e/.output/sf-e2e-3/results/out-net-18-soak*.json and soak-*.csv (nodes, removed_videos_alive per minute); reproduce without the probe with a plain context and the Runtime.queryObjects count above
OUT-11.fix: In MediaView.dispose() for device sources: video.pause(); video.srcObject = null (after provider.detach) and video.load(); the same for the fallback media and for videos handed to MediaPool.disposeRest().

OUT-07.title: docs/testing.md 1.7 / GAP-24 pin hooks and a debug overlay format the output page does not have: no data-state, data-source, data-slate, slate-title/-subtitle or debug-overlay test ids; the overlay is <pre class="c-debug"> with German lines
OUT-07.actual: Only data-item-id and data-scene-id exist. The specs derive the item state from the computed styles the renderer toggles (hold-frame canvas shown = hold, .sf-r-held shown = held, .sf-r-fallback shown = fallback; support/output/browser/output-probe.js) and read the overlay as it is: «<Produktion> · Szene «Name»», «Revision n · Sendung live», «Hub verbunden · Sync aktuell», «LiveKit verbunden», «Latenz ≈ n ms · Renderer n fps», «K1 Name · 1280×720 · 30 fps · 1,7 Mbit/s · Verlust 0,0 % · Puffer 31 ms». Update the plan or add the attributes.

OUT-08.title: The output reports the animation frame rate of the page (about 60 fps) as OutputReport.fps and the popover says «1920 × 1080 · 30 fps»; E2E-OUT-20 expects 20-31
OUT-08.steps: Observe the Report invocations of the output hub for 12 s.
OUT-08.expected: E2E-OUT-20: fps between 20 and 31 (the 30 fps of the program).
OUT-08.actual: FpsMeter counts requestAnimationFrame callbacks, so the report is 60 on a 60 Hz display regardless of the content. The spec asserts 20..144. Whether «fps» should mean the page's frame rate or the program's is open; the number says nothing about dropped video frames (use the decoded frame rate).

OUT-09.title: E2E-OUT-15 expects a main-thread-blocked output page to turn «stale»; the API drops its hub connection after 5 s, so the Regie shows «nicht verbunden» (state none) after about 3.5-5.3 s and the page reconnects at once when it runs again
OUT-09.steps: Block the main thread of the output page for 10 s (busy loop) while watching GET /snapshot outputStatus.
OUT-09.expected: E2E-OUT-15: state stale after <= 8 s, connected again afterwards.
OUT-09.actual: States: connected -> none/0 consumers (+3.5 to +5.3 s, SignalR client timeout 5 s < Output:StaleAfter 6 s) -> connected (about 0.2 s after the block ended). «stale» is only reachable by a connected hub client that stops reporting (asserted with a silent Node hub client: lamp warning, «verbunden, kein aktuelles Bild»).

OUT-10.title: E2E-OUT-02 expects no audio receiver on any peer connection; LiveKit negotiates three receive-only audio transceivers (muted, no RTP) and three video transceivers up front
OUT-10.steps: Open the output with a camera on air and list peer.getReceivers() / getStats().
OUT-10.actual: 3 audio receivers (all muted, no inbound-rtp audio, no bytes). The spec asserts that no audio track carries data and no audio RTP stream exists.
